title: Grade 5 Math — Fri, Jun 20
description: Data Handling — Day 5 of 5: Mixed synthesis — full week review
subject: mathematics

questions.question: In a tally mark, one group of five is represented as:
questions.explanation: Four vertical strokes and one diagonal crossing them = 5. This is the standard tally mark for 5.

questions.question: A pictograph uses key: ★ = 10. A row has 4½ stars. The value is:
In a bar graph, what does the height of a bar represent?
options: The frequency or value for that category
questions.explanation: The height of each bar corresponds to the value/frequency for that category as read on the y-axis.

questions.question: Find the MODE: 2, 5, 3, 5, 2, 5, 3, 2, 5
questions.explanation: 5 appears 4 times; 2 appears 3 times; 3 appears 2 times. Mode = 5.

questions.question: Bar graph: Trees planted — Oak=40, Pine=60, Mango=50, Neem=30. What is the mean number of trees planted?
Same tree data (Oak=40, Pine=60, Mango=50, Neem=30). What is the median?
questions.explanation: Arrange: 30, 40, 50, 60. Two middle values: 40 and 50. Median = (40+50)÷2 = 45.

questions.question: If 5 students scored an average (mean) of 70, what is the total of all their scores?
questions.explanation: Mean = Total ÷ Count → Total = Mean × Count = 70 × 5 = 350.

questions.question: Which average is BEST to use when comparing the 'most common' shoe size?
questions.explanation: Mode is best for 'most common' — it tells you which item occurs most frequently. Shoe sizes are categorical, so mode is appropriate.

questions.question: Which average might be distorted by one very large value?
questions.explanation: An outlier (extreme value) pulls the mean toward it, making it unrepresentative. Median is not affected much by outliers.

questions.question: Frequency table: Colour — Red:5, Blue:8, Green:3, Yellow:4. Draw a bar graph — which bar would be TALLEST?
questions.explanation: Blue has the highest frequency (8) → tallest bar.

questions.question: Same colour data (Red:5, Blue:8, Green:3, Yellow:4). If the scale goes up by 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8), which value doesn't land exactly on a gridline?
questions.explanation: Scale 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. Red = 5 falls between 4 and 6 — it does not land on a gridline. The bar must be drawn halfway between.

questions.question: A dataset has values: 10, 20, 30, 100. The mean is 40. Does the mean represent the data well?
options: Yes — the mean is always the best measure
No — the outlier 100 pulls the mean up to 40, which isn't representative of most values
questions.explanation: Mean = (10+20+30+100)÷4 = 160÷4 = 40. But 3 out of 4 values are below 40. The outlier 100 distorts the mean. Median = (20+30)÷2 = 25 would be more representative.

questions.question: WEEK STAR: A class of 6 students scored: 55, 65, 70, 70, 75, 85. Find: (a) mean, (b) median, (c) mode.
questions.explanation: (a) Mean: Sum=55+65+70+70+75+85=420. Mean=420÷6=70. (b) Median: 6 values, middle two = 70,70. Median=(70+70)÷2=70. (c) Mode: 70 appears twice. Mode=70. All three = 70!
